statutory.summary: Across the boroughs whose returns allow the comparison, a leased home cost around £61 a household a night in both 2023-24 and 2024-25, while nightly-paid accommodation rose from around £70 to £94. After rent recovered, moving a household from nightly-paid accommodation to a leased home saved around £39 a night in 2024-25, roughly £14,000 a year, up from around £22 the year before. The saving may be smaller than it appears, because some leased homes are held by housing associations whose costs the council’s accounts do not show.
statutory.disagreements: Of the boroughs filing household returns, about half file at least one category differently in their accounts and their household return. Figures by category are shown only where the two agree; the pooled figure for all purchased temporary accommodation is shown for every borough with a return.

london.leasing_gap_corroboration: Havering reaches the same conclusion from its own books: its cabinet papers put the gap between nightly-let and leased placements at £24,000 per family per year (22 January 2025). Havering’s statutory returns support that figure, and show it to be about double the London average: Havering is the widest gap in London, not the typical one.
